standard_prerequisites.name: H-space
standard_prerequisites.statement: An H-space is a pointed type with a multiplication mu, a unit e and the unit laws mu(e,a) = a and mu(a,e) = a.
standard_prerequisites.use: The unit laws are used at source line 1348 to identify mu(e,-) with the identity.

standard_prerequisites.name: Connected type
standard_prerequisites.statement: A is connected when trunc 0 A is contractible.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what makes the family over trunc 0 A trivial at the basepoint.

standard_prerequisites.name: Truncation of a proposition-valued family
standard_prerequisites.statement: Since prop is a set, a family P : A -> prop descends to a family P' : trunc 0 A -> prop with P'(|a|_0) := P(a).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the descent performed at source lines 1343-1345.

core_obligations: Reduce to the first statement, since the other is symmetric (source lines 1336-1337).
Observe that 'mu(a,-) is an equivalence' is a proposition-valued family P : A -> prop, so that proving it means producing a section (source lines 1339-1341).
Use that prop is a set to descend P to a family P' on trunc 0 A with P'(|a|_0) := P(a) (source lines 1343-1344).

Since A is connected, trunc 0 A is contractible, so a section of P' need only be produced at the basepoint |e|_0, where P'(|e|_0) = P(e) holds because mu(e,-) is the identity map by the unit law (source lines 1345-1349).
Conclude that P'(x) holds for every x : trunc 0 A, hence P(a) for every a : A (source lines 1351-1353).

proof_roadmap.step: Turn the equivalence statement into a proposition-valued family and a section problem.
Descend the family along 0-truncation and use connectedness.
Discharge the section at the basepoint by the unit law.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the unlabelled lemma at source lines 1330-1333, original Lemma 8.5.5: on a connected H-space both translations mu(a,-) and mu(-,a) are equivalences. The author's proof (source lines 1335-1354) is not a direct computation but a descent argument: the statement that a translation is an equivalence is a proposition-valued family, so proving it means producing a section (lines 1339-1341), and since the universe of propositions is a set the family descends along 0-truncation to a family on trunc 0 A (lines 1343-1344). Connectedness makes trunc 0 A contractible, so it suffices to inhabit the fiber at the basepoint, where the unit law of the H-space identifies the translation with the identity (lines 1345-1349). The last two lines transfer the result back along the truncation. The statement gives no hint that the argument goes through truncation and contractibility.
